Tools and tips

Practical advice on security, recovery, AI and cloud.

Cyber security

Turn on multi-factor authentication

Require it for email, admin accounts and remote access first.

Patch on a schedule

Fix critical and high CVSS findings first, on endpoints and servers alike.

Treat unexpected links and attachments as suspect

Report suspicious email instead of deleting it so others are protected too.

Limit privileged access

Give people only the access they need and review admin accounts regularly.

Backup and recovery

Follow 3-2-1

Keep three copies on two types of media, with one copy offsite.

Keep one copy offline or immutable

Ransomware cannot encrypt what it cannot reach.

Test restores, not just backup jobs

A green backup job does not prove you can recover.

Write down RTO and RPO

Agree how long each key system can be down and how much data you can lose.

AI at work

Keep confidential data out of public AI tools

Provide approved tools and make the rule clear to staff.

Use DLP to catch sensitive data before it leaves

Classify data and set policies for uploads, paste and email.

Verify AI output before acting on it

Treat it as a draft, especially for code, contracts and figures.

Review what AI assistants and agents can access

Apply least privilege and sensitivity labels to the data they reach.

Cloud and devices

Enrol every device in management

Require encryption, screen lock and up-to-date software.

Use conditional access

Only compliant devices and verified users reach company data.

Review cloud costs monthly

Remove unused resources and right-size what remains.

Keep an inventory

Know your devices, software, licences and who owns each.
